dervis-irab:1-10.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْمَعارِجِ) the ascents (al-maṣāʿid), plural of مَعْرَج.
(المهل): the dregs of oil, or molten silver; it was mentioned before in Sūrat al-Dukhān.
(العهن) wool in general, without restriction, or wool dyed red, or dyed in various colours; these are different views.

* I'rab:
(سَأَلَ سائِلٌ بِعَذابٍ واقِعٍ) سأل is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, containing the meaning of دعا ("called for"), and for that reason it was made transitive the way that verb is; سائل is its agent (fāʿil); بعذاب is attached to (mutaʿalliq) سأل, and واقع is an adjective (naʿt). It is also said that it is in its own sense and the bāʾ has the meaning of عن ("about"); Abū al-Baqāʾ chose this. Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī said: «If it is from questioning (al-suʾāl), then its basis is to take two objects, and it is permissible to limit it to one of them; and if it is limited to one of them, it may take it by means of a preposition, so the implied form would be: a questioner asked Allah, or the Prophet ﷺ, or the Muslims, بعذاب, i.e. about a punishment». The questioner is al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, when he said: "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down stones upon us from the sky or bring us a painful punishment"; he was among those killed on the day of Badr. Al-Wāḥidī said: «The bāʾ in بعذاب is for emphasis, as in His words وهزي إليك بجذع النخلة, and the meaning is: a questioner asked for a punishment that will befall». (لِلْكافِرينَ لَيْسَ لَهُ دافِعٌ) Concerning the preposition and its genitive noun there are several views. The first is that it is attached to سأل as containing the meaning of دعا, i.e. he called for it upon them. The second is that it is attached to واقع and the lām is causal, i.e. descending because of them. The third is that the lām has the meaning of على, i.e. befalling the disbelievers; on this view it is also attached to واقع. The clause ليس له دافع is a second adjective of عذاب, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from عذاب because it is qualified. ليس is a defective past verb, له is its fronted khabar (predicate) and دافع its delayed noun. (مِنَ اللَّهِ ذِي الْمَعارِجِ) attached to واقع, i.e. befalling from Him and from His direction; or attached to دافع, meaning that there is none to repel it from His side when its time comes. ذي المعارج is an adjective of الله. (تَعْرُجُ الْمَلائِكَةُ وَالرُّوحُ إِلَيْهِ فِي يَوْمٍ كانَ مِقْدارُهُ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ) a resumptive statement, set out to emphasise the far-reaching loftiness. تعرج الملائكة is an imperfect verb and its agent; الروح is conjoined to الملائكة, and by it is meant Jibrīl, so it is a conjoining of the particular to the general. إليه is attached to تعرج; في يوم is attached to an omitted element indicated by واقع, i.e. the punishment befalls them on the Day of Resurrection. Kāna and its noun, and خمسين is its khabar; ألف سنة is the tamyīz (specification) of خمسين. Or [في يوم] is also attached to تعرج. (فَاصْبِرْ صَبْراً جَمِيلًا) The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ, i.e. if you have known this and pondered its import, then be patient. اصبر is an imperative verb and its agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta"; صبرا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and جميلا an adjective. (إِنَّهُمْ يَرَوْنَهُ بَعِيداً) Inna and its noun, and the clause يرونه is its khabar; the pronoun is for the punishment; بعيدا is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because the seeing is cognitive. The clause is causal and has no grammatical position. (وَنَراهُ قَرِيباً) conjoined to the previous clause and falling within the scope of the khabar. (يَوْمَ تَكُونُ السَّماءُ كَالْمُهْلِ) The adverb is attached to قريبا, or to an omitted element indicated by واقع, i.e. it befalls on the day when … The clause تكون is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being put in construct with it; السماء is its noun and كالمهل its khabar. (وَتَكُونُ الْجِبالُ كَالْعِهْنِ) conjoined to the previous clause and parallel to it in its i'rab. (وَلا يَسْئَلُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيماً) The wāw is a conjunction and lā is negative; يسأل حميم is an imperfect verb and its agent; حميما is the first object of يسأل, and the second object is omitted, its implied form being "his intercession and his help". It is also said that حميما is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), and يسأل then has no need of an object.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «يوم تعرج الملائكة والروح إليه في يوم كان مقداره خمسين ألف سنة» [Translator's note: the source quotes the verse with an initial «يوم», which is not in the Quranic text (تعرج الملائكة والروح إليه في يوم كان مقداره خمسين ألف سنة)] there is the device of figurative representation (tamthīl). What is meant is not the literal reality of that number; rather, what is meant is an indication that it will appear long to the disbeliever because of the terror and hardships he meets during it. So there is no contradiction with the verse of al-Sajda «في يوم كان مقداره ألف سنة». The Arabs describe days of hardship as long and days of joy as short. A poet said:
فقصارهنّ مع الهموم طويلة ... وطوالهنّ مع السرور قصار
(Their short ones, amid cares, are long, and their long ones, amid joy, are short.)
And another said:
ويوم كظل الرمح قصر طوله ... دم الزق عنا واصطفاق المزاهر
(And a day like the shadow of a spear, whose length was shortened for us by the blood of the wineskin and the clapping of lutes.)
2- In His words «يوم تكون السماء كالمهل» there is an unqualified simile (tashbīh mursal), and the point of resemblance is the changing of colour; likewise His words «وتكون الجبال كالعهن», where the point of resemblance is the flying about and scattering. Abū al-ʿAlāʾ cast his eyes on this lofty sky of eloquence when he said, lamenting his father:
فيا ليت شعري هل يخفّ وقاره ... إذا صار أحد في القيامة كالعهن
(Would that I knew: will his dignity grow light when Uḥud becomes like carded wool on the Day of Resurrection?)

dervis-irab:11-23.t:
* Vocabulary:
«وفصيلته» al-faṣīla is the clan (al-ʿashīra). Thaʿlab said: the nearest forefathers. It is a faʿīla with the meaning of a mafʿūla, i.e. one from whom [he] was separated.
(لَظى) a name of Hell, because it تتلظّى, i.e. blazes upon whoever roasts in it.
(لِلشَّوى) al-shawā is the plural of shawāt, which is the skin of the head (the scalp).

* I'rab:
(يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ يَوَدُّ الْمُجْرِمُ لَوْ يَفْتَدِي مِنْ عَذابِ يَوْمِئِذٍ بِبَنِيهِ) The clause is resumptive or circumstantial; al-Zamakhsharī permitted it to be an adjective, i.e. "a close friend made to see [them]". يبصرونهم is an imperfect passive verb; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) and the hāʾ is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). It was made to reach a second object by the doubling [of the middle radical], and the first object stood in place of the agent. The two pronouns in يبصرونهم were made plural, though they are for the two close friends, by construing them according to the meaning of generality, because they are two indefinite nouns in a negative context. In this there is evidence that the agent and the object occurring in a negative context are general, just as it was held regarding the words "By Allah, I will not drink water from a leather flask" that it covers all waters and all flasks, contrary to some regarding the flask. That is, the healthy ones are shown one another and recognise one another, but they do not exchange words because they are preoccupied with themselves. يود المجرم is an imperfect verb and its agent, and the clause is circumstantial; law is maṣdariyya with the meaning of an, because it occurs after a verb of wishing, and together with what falls in its scope it is an interpreted maṣdar, the object of يودّ, i.e. he wishes a ransoming. من عذاب is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يفتدي. يومئذ are two adverbs in construct, and the tanwīn is a substitute for omitted clauses, the implied form being: on the day when the sky becomes like molten metal, the mountains become like wool, and no close friend asks a close friend. ببنيه is also attached to يفتدي. (وَصاحِبَتِهِ وَأَخِيهِ وَفَصِيلَتِهِ الَّتِي تُؤْوِيهِ) conjoined to بنيه; the clause تؤويه is the ṣila (relative clause), i.e. which embraces him in lineage. (وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعاً ثُمَّ يُنْجِيهِ) also conjoined; في الأرض is the ṣila of the relative noun, and جميعا is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ثم is a conjunction of delay, on account of the severity of the terror; ينجيه is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object, i.e. he wishes that he could ransom himself and then that the ransom would save him. Thumma is for the remoteness of the saving; that is, he wishes that all these were within reach of his hand and that he could give them up in ransom for himself; but how far that is! (كَلَّا إِنَّها لَظى) كلا is a particle of rebuff and deterrence against their wish to ransom themselves, and an alert that that wish is not admissible and is of no avail. Inna and its noun, and لظى is its khabar (predicate); the pronoun is for the Fire, indicated by "the punishment". (نَزَّاعَةً لِلشَّوى) an emphatic or clarifying ḥāl, or it is accusative by specification (ikhtiṣāṣ) for intimidation. On the ḥāl view, what governs it is the verbal meaning indicated by لظى, i.e. it blazes as a stripper [of the scalp]. It was also read in the nominative, so it is a second khabar, i.e. [or] the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is a stripper"; it is said it is a badal (substitute) from لظى; it is said both are khabars; and it is said لظى is a badal from the noun of inna and نزّاعة is its khabar. (تَدْعُوا مَنْ أَدْبَرَ وَتَوَلَّى) The clause is a ḥāl from the pronoun in نزّاعة; the agent of تدعو is latent, referring to لظى; من is a relative noun, the direct object; the clause أدبر has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila, and تولّى is conjoined to أدبر. Further clarification of this calling will come in the section on rhetoric. (وَجَمَعَ فَأَوْعى) conjoined to أدبر and تولّى. The meaning of أوعى is: he amassed wealth, put it in a container (wiʿāʾ) and hoarded it, and did not pay with it the right of Allah the Exalted. (إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعاً) The clause serves as the reason for what preceded. Inna and its noun; the al in الإنسان is generic; the clause خلق is the khabar of inna and the deputy agent is latent, referring to الإنسان; هلوعا is a prospective ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because he is not characterised by these qualities before his birth and at the time of his creation. (إِذا مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ جَزُوعاً) إذا is an adverb attached to جزوعا; the clause مسّه is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being put in construct with it; الشر is the agent; جزوعا is a ḥāl from the pronoun in هلوعا, and you may make it an adjective of هلوعا. (وَإِذا مَسَّهُ الْخَيْرُ مَنُوعاً) conjoined to the previous clause and parallel to it in its i'rab. (إِلَّا الْمُصَلِّينَ) an exception from الإنسان, by which the genus is meant, so it is a connected exception. (الَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلى صَلاتِهِمْ دائِمُونَ) الذين is an adjective of المصلين; هم is a mubtadaʾ; على صلاتهم is attached to دائمون, and دائمون is their khabar; the nominal clause is the ṣila of الذين.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «تدعو من أدبر وتولى» there is a rational metaphor (majāz ʿaqlī) for bringing them forth, as though it calls them and brings them forth — the discussion of rational metaphor has preceded in this book — or an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya). Of this kind is the saying of Dhū al-Rumma describing a wild bull:
أمسى بوهبين مجتازا لمرتعه ... من ذي الفوارس تدعو أنفه الربب
(At evening he was at Wahbayn, passing on to his pasture from Dhū al-Fawāris, the first sprouts calling his nose.)
Wahbayn is the name of a place, and likewise Dhū al-Fawāris. الربب, with two bāʾs, is the plural of rubba, which is the first pasture-grass to sprout. Al-duʿāʾ is requesting, and here it is a metaphor for causing the matter, because the small plants are the cause of his nose reaching the ground to graze on them. The calling may also be of the type of metaphor (istiʿāra): the sprouts are likened to a caller, the thing likened to is omitted, and something of its characteristics is taken.
Also of this kind is the saying of Dhū al-Rumma:
ليالي اللهو يطبيني فأتبعه ... كأنني ضارب في غمرة لعب
(Nights when amusement calls me and I follow it, as though I were a swimmer in a deep flood, playing.)
ليالي is accusative as an adverb; اللهو is a mubtadaʾ; طباه يطبوه ويطبيه when he calls him and draws him. That is, amusement calls me on many nights and I follow it, as though I were swimming in a deep expanse of water that covers a man's height. لعب is a second khabar. The adverb is attached to يطبيني, and it is said it is attached to what precedes it, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being put in construct with it.

dervis-irab:24-35.t:
* I'rab:
(وَالَّذِينَ فِي أَمْوالِهِمْ حَقٌّ مَعْلُومٌ) والذين is conjoined to the first الذين; في أموالهم is a fronted khabar (predicate) and حق a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); معلوم is an adjective (naʿt). What is meant by it is the obligatory zakāt. The nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (لِلسَّائِلِ وَالْمَحْرُومِ) an adjective of حق. (وَالَّذِينَ يُصَدِّقُونَ بِيَوْمِ الدِّينِ) also conjoined; the clause يصدقون is the ṣila of the relative noun, and بيوم الدين is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يصدقون, i.e. the Day of Recompense. (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ مِنْ عَذابِ رَبِّهِمْ مُشْفِقُونَ) also conjoined; هم is a mubtadaʾ and مشفقون its khabar; من عذاب ربهم is attached to His word مشفقون; the clause is the ṣila. (إِنَّ عَذابَ رَبِّهِمْ غَيْرُ مَأْمُونٍ) The clause gives the reason for the fearing. Inna and its noun, and غير مأمون is its khabar. (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حافِظُونَ) also conjoined; هم is a mubtadaʾ and حافظون its khabar; لفروجهم is attached to حافظون, i.e. [guarding them] from the unlawful and forbidden. (إِلَّا عَلى أَزْواجِهِمْ أَوْ ما مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ) إلا is a particle of exception, and على أزواجهم is an exception from the most general of states; aw is a conjunction and ما is conjoined to أزواجهم; the clause ملكت is the ṣila and أيمانهم is the fāʿil (agent). What is meant by ما ملكت أيمانهم is slave-women. فإنهم: the fāʾ is a conjunction; inna and its noun, and غير ملومين is its khabar. (فَمَنِ ابْتَغى وَراءَ ذلِكَ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ العادُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; من is a conditional noun causing the jussive, a mubtadaʾ; ابتغى is a past verb in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and its agent is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to من. وراء is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ابتغى, وراء having left its adverbial use, i.e. he sought what is beyond that, namely enjoyment by marriage and by what the right hand possesses. You may also keep it adverbial and attach it to an omitted element that is an adjective of the omitted direct object, i.e. whoever seeks a matter that lies beyond that. The fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); أولئك is a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), and العادون is the khabar of أولئك; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. You may also make هم a second mubtadaʾ and العادون its khabar, the clause being the khabar of أولئك. (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِأَماناتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ راعُونَ) conjoined to what preceded; هم is a mubtadaʾ and راعون its khabar; لأماناتهم is attached to راعون; the nominal clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ بِشَهاداتِهِمْ قائِمُونَ) also conjoined; in one reading it is in the singular. (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلى صَلاتِهِمْ يُحافِظُونَ) also conjoined. (أُولئِكَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ مُكْرَمُونَ) أولئك is a mubtadaʾ, في جنات a khabar and مكرمون a second khabar; you may also attach في جنات to مكرمون.

* Rhetoric:
In the repetition of the prayer there is an evident hyperbole, out of concern for its importance and to extol its merit. Added to the repetition are: opening the clause with the pronoun and building the clause upon it, putting the preposition and its genitive noun before the verb, and the khabar's being a verbal clause. The nominal clause conveys permanence and continuity, and the verbal clause conveys renewal together with continuity. This is a wondrous pattern unique to the Book of Allah.

dervis-irab:36-44.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُهْطِعِينَ) hastening towards you, stretching out their necks, turning their gazes towards you. It is one of the words whose explanation needs whole sentences. In al-Qāmūs:
«هطع, like منع, هَطْعًا and هُطُوعًا: he hastened forward in fear, and turned his gaze on a thing, not taking it off it. هطع: he stretched out his neck and lowered his head, like استهطع. Like أمير [i.e. هطيع]: the wide road. Like محسن [i.e. مُهطِع]: one who looks in abasement and submission, not taking his gaze away; or the silent one who sets off towards whoever called him. A مُهطِع camel is one with a natural downward slope in its neck». The explanation of this root has preceded in Sūrat Ibrāhīm.
(عِزِينَ) plural of عِزَة. Abū ʿUbayda said: groups in dispersion. It is said: a small gathering, such as three by three and four by four. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: "In the house there are عزون", i.e. various sorts of people. Al-Kumayt said:
ونحن وجندل باغ تركنا ... كتائب جندل شتّى عزينا
(We — and Jandal was the aggressor — left the troops of Jandal scattered in separate bands.)
عِزَة is one of the words whose final radical has been dropped. It is said it is a wāw and its origin is عِزْوَة, as though each group traces its descent (taʿtazī) to someone other than the one the other group traces its descent to, so they are dispersed; one says عزاه يعزوه when he attributes him to someone else. It is said its final radical is a hāʾ and the origin is عِزْهَة. عزة was given the plural with wāw and nūn just as سنة and its sisters were given the plural with them. It is also said it is a yāʾ, since one says عزيته, with yāʾ, أعزيه, with the meaning of عزوته. The discussion of what is attached to the sound masculine plural has preceded.
(نُصُبٍ) The discussion of it has preceded in detail, and we add here that it was read نَصْب, with fatḥa and sukūn; our reading is with two ḍammas; it was read with two fatḥas; and it was read with ḍamma then sukūn. The first is a singular noun with the meaning of the set-up marker towards which a person hastens. Abū ʿAmr said: it is the hunter's net, to which he hastens when game falls into it, for fear of its escaping. As for the second, it admits three views: first, that it is a singular noun with the meaning of an idol set up for worship; second, that it is the plural of نِصاب, like كُتُب, the plural of كتاب; third, that it is the plural of نَصْب, like رُهُن from رَهْن and سُقُف from سَقْف, and the plural of the plural is أنصاب. As for the third, it is a faʿal with the meaning of a mafʿūl, i.e. set up (manṣūb), like القَبَض with the meaning of المقبوض. The fourth is a lightened form of the second.
(يُوفِضُونَ) hastening to the caller, racing one another.

* I'rab:
(فَمالِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا قِبَلَكَ مُهْطِعِينَ) The fāʾ is resumptive; ما is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and للذين is the khabar (predicate) of ما, i.e. what is it that has befallen them and driven them to look at you and to disperse? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray at the Kaʿba and recite the Qur'an, and they would gather round him in circle after circle, listening and mocking his words, and saying: "If these enter Paradise as Muhammad says, we shall surely enter it before them"; so [this verse] was revealed. قبلك is an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), or to مهطعين, i.e. being in the direction that adjoins you, on the right and on the left. مهطعين is a ḥāl from الذين. (عَنِ الْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ الشِّمالِ عِزِينَ) The preposition and its genitive noun is also a ḥāl from the relative noun; it is said it is attached to مهطعين. عزين is also a ḥāl from the relative noun, so the four are ḥāls from the relative noun. It is also said it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in مهطعين, so it would be an overlapping ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila). Abū al-Baqāʾ attached عن اليمين وعن الشمال to عزين, and some parsed عزين as an adjective of مهطعين. (أَيَطْمَعُ كُلُّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ أَنْ يُدْخَلَ جَنَّةَ نَعِيمٍ) The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval; يطمع is an imperfect verb and كل امرئ its fāʿil (agent); منهم is an adjective of امرئ. An and what falls in its scope is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to يطمع, i.e. does he covet entering? The nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of يدخل is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa", and جنة نعيم is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), by extension of usage. (كَلَّا إِنَّا خَلَقْناهُمْ مِمَّا يَعْلَمُونَ) كلا is a particle of rebuff and deterrence against their Ashʿab-like greed to enter Paradise [Translator's note: Ashʿab was a proverbial figure of greed]. The clause إنا خلقناهم gives the reason for the rebuff. Inna and its noun, and the clause خلقناهم is its khabar; مما is attached to خلقناهم, and the clause يعلمون is the ṣila (relative clause). The meaning is that they are created from a filthy drop of fluid that does not befit the world of holiness; so whoever has not adorned himself with faith, washed away the filth from himself with righteous deeds and added the perfections, is not worthy of entering the Gardens. Or it is an inference from the first creation to the second creation, and that the One who was able to create the first time is not incapable of bringing back. (فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ الْمَشارِقِ وَالْمَغارِبِ إِنَّا لَقادِرُونَ) The fāʾ is resumptive and lā is redundant (zāʾida); أقسم is an imperfect verb and its agent is latent, its implied form being "anā"; برب المشارق والمغارب is attached to أقسم. The clause إنا لقادرون has no grammatical position because it is the answer of the oath; inna and its noun, the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and قادرون is its khabar. (عَلى أَنْ نُبَدِّلَ خَيْراً مِنْهُمْ وَما نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ) An and what falls in its scope is in the position of the genitive by على, and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to قادرون; خيرا is the object of نبدل and منهم is attached to خيرا. The wāw is a conjunction; mā is Ḥijāzī and نحن is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition and مسبوقين is genitive in form and accusative in position as its khabar. The clause is conjoined to the answer of the oath and falls within what is sworn upon. (فَذَرْهُمْ يَخُوضُوا وَيَلْعَبُوا حَتَّى يُلاقُوا يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ) The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ, i.e. since it has become clear that bringing down upon them what We wish does not escape Us nor is beyond Our power, then leave them. ذرهم is an imperative verb whose past tense has died out, with a latent agent and a direct object; يخوضوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer of the command; يلعبوا is conjoined to يخوضوا. حتى is a particle of limit and of the genitive; يلاقوا is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after حتى, and the wāw is the agent; يومهم is the direct object and الذي an adjective of يومهم; the clause يوعدون is the ṣila of the relative noun; it is an imperfect passive verb and the wāw is the deputy agent. (يَوْمَ يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ الْأَجْداثِ سِراعاً كَأَنَّهُمْ إِلى نُصُبٍ يُوفِضُونَ)
يوم is a badal (substitute) from يومهم; the clause يخرجون is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being put in construct with it; من الأجداث is attached to يخرجون; سراعا is a ḥāl from the wāw; the clause كأنهم is a second ḥāl, also from the wāw, so they would be successive ḥāls (mutarādifa), or from the pronoun in سراعا, so it would be an overlapping ḥāl. Kaʾanna and its noun; إلى نصب is attached to يوفضون, and the clause يوفضون is the khabar of كأنهم. (خاشِعَةً أَبْصارُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ ذلِكَ الْيَوْمُ الَّذِي كانُوا يُوعَدُونَ) خاشعة is a ḥāl from the agent of يوفضون or from the agent of يخرجون, the first being closer; أبصارهم is the agent of خاشعة. The clause ترهقهم ذلة is a second ḥāl, and you may make it resumptive. ذلك is a mubtadaʾ and اليوم its khabar, and الذي is an adjective; kāna and its noun, and the clause يوعدون is its khabar, and the clause is the ṣila. The clause ذلك اليوم is resumptive or explicative; in either case it has no grammatical position.
